review_evidence: Codex self-review: title-theme alignment, original honesty narrative, Class 4 evidence and grammar depth, and unseen assessment forms
Focused checks: canonical hash, key-option consistency, passage freshness, assessment coverage, and chapter/corpus quality
title: The Tinkling Bells
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Read the choice behind the bell
levels.focus: identify the main idea and evidence in an honesty narrative
levels.teaching_goal: State the moral focus of a paragraph and cite the choice that reveals it.

guided_check.teaching_block: A moral story's main idea comes from the important choice, not from the object in the story. Returning money shows honesty.
guided_check.passage: Naman had saved for a tinkling bicycle bell. At the market, a seller returned fifty rupees too much. Naman noticed the error and gave the note back before buying the bell.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence captures the moral focus of Naman's choice?
options: Naman acts honestly when he returns extra change.
Naman likes the sound of bells.
accepted_answers: Naman acts honestly when he returns extra change.

bridge.teaching_block: Separate the situation, choice, and result. The choice is the strongest evidence for the character's value.
bridge.passage: Lina found a silver anklet with tiny bells near the well. She carried it to the village office, where its owner later collected it.
bridge.prompt: Which action is evidence of Lina's honesty?
options: She took the anklet to the village office.
accepted_answers: She took the anklet to the village office.

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is calling a character honest only because the ending is happy. Honesty is shown by a truthful action even when no reward follows.
masterclass.passage: A shop assistant forgot to charge Yusuf for a packet of bells. Yusuf checked the bill and pointed out the missing item.
options: He reports a mistake that benefits him.
accepted_answers: He reports a mistake that benefits him.

independent_check.teaching_block: Find the moral focus and evidence in this unseen event.
independent_check.passage: Mira borrowed a costume belt for the school play. One bell came loose during rehearsal. She told the teacher immediately and offered to help repair it.
independent_check.prompt: State the main idea and support it with Mira's action.

concept_slots.description: states that Mira is honest or responsible about damage
mentions that she told the teacher and/or offered repair

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same evidence method in a digital setting.
transfer_check.passage: Aarush saw that an online quiz had shown him the answer to the next question by mistake. He closed the page and informed his teacher before continuing.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain what Aarush's choice shows and cite the clue.

concept_slots.description: identifies honesty, fairness, or integrity
mentions closing the page or telling the teacher

levels.title: Track problem, choice, and result
levels.focus: sequence events and explain how one event causes the next
levels.teaching_goal: Use time and cause clues to place narrative events in a logical order.

guided_check.teaching_block: Sequence a story by asking what must happen first. A child must notice a lost object before deciding to return it.
guided_check.passage: First, Asha heard a bell under a bench. Next, she found a pet's collar. Then she read the address tag and returned the collar.
guided_check.prompt: What happened directly after Asha heard the bell?

bridge.teaching_block: Time words are useful, but logic also matters. Finding an owner must come before handing the object back.
bridge.passage: Events: (1) Ketu gave the pouch to its owner. (2) Ketu saw a name inside the pouch. (3) Ketu picked up the pouch.
options: Ketu gave the pouch to its owner.
Ketu saw a name inside the pouch.

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not assume the order in which choices are listed is the story order. Use cause: checking the receipt must happen before correcting the bill.
masterclass.passage: Ravi paid for a bell, checked his receipt, noticed an unpaid string, and returned to the counter.
masterclass.prompt: Which event made Ravi return to the counter?

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange the fresh events without time-word support.
independent_check.passage: Events: the librarian thanked Pooja; Pooja noticed an extra book in her bag; Pooja returned the book.
independent_check.prompt: Put the three events in story order.
accepted_answers: Pooja noticed an extra book in her bag, Pooja returned the book, the librarian thanked Pooja
Pooja noticed an extra book in her bag; Pooja returned the book; the librarian thanked Pooja
noticed extra book, returned book, librarian thanked Pooja

transfer_check.teaching_block: Sequence a cause-and-result chain in sport.
transfer_check.passage: Events: the referee corrected the score; Iqbal admitted the ball touched his hand; the other team questioned the point.
transfer_check.prompt: Put the events in the most logical order.
accepted_answers: the other team questioned the point, Iqbal admitted the ball touched his hand, the referee corrected the score
the other team questioned the point; Iqbal admitted the ball touched his hand; the referee corrected the score
team questioned, Iqbal admitted, referee corrected

levels.title: Use contrast to unlock words
levels.focus: infer meanings and opposites from sentence context
levels.teaching_goal: Use contrast markers and outcomes to identify a word's meaning and a legitimate opposite.

guided_check.teaching_block: But often signals a contrast. If the bell was faint before but loud after repair, faint means quiet or hard to hear.
guided_check.passage: The old bell sounded faint, but after cleaning it rang loudly.
guided_check.prompt: Which word is opposite in meaning to faint here?

bridge.teaching_block: Find the two ideas placed against each other. Reluctant contrasts with eager in the next sentence.
bridge.passage: Sumi was reluctant to admit the mistake at first, but soon she was eager to tell the truth.
bridge.prompt: What does reluctant most nearly mean?

masterclass.teaching_block: An opposite must fit the sentence's meaning and grammar. The opposite of honest is dishonest, not honesty, because the sentence needs a describing word.
masterclass.passage: The honest customer corrected the bill; a _____ customer might hide the error.

independent_check.teaching_block: Infer the opposite from the new context.
independent_check.passage: The crowded lane became deserted after the shops closed.
independent_check.prompt: Write the opposite of crowded as used here.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a contrast clue in a weather report.
transfer_check.passage: The morning was gloomy, yet by afternoon the sky looked bright and cheerful.
transfer_check.prompt: Which word in the sentence is the best opposite of gloomy?

levels.title: Compare sounds and choices accurately
levels.focus: use comparative and superlative adjectives in context
levels.teaching_goal: Use comparative forms for two and superlative forms for three or more while preserving sentence meaning.

guided_check.teaching_block: Use -er or more when comparing two. The brass bell is louder than the clay bell.
guided_check.passage: A brass bell rings loudly. A clay bell makes a soft sound.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence compares the two correctly?
options: The brass bell is louder than the clay bell.
The brass bell is loudest than the clay bell.
The clay bell is more softest.
accepted_answers: The brass bell is louder than the clay bell.

bridge.teaching_block: Count the things being compared. Three or more usually call for a superlative such as smallest.
bridge.passage: Three bells weigh 80 g, 110 g, and 140 g.
bridge.prompt: Which phrase describes the 80 g bell?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common error is using both more and -er. Say kinder, not more kinder; say more careful, not carefuller.
masterclass.passage: Rina returned a lost purse, while another child ignored it.
options: Rina made the more kinder choice.
Rina made the kindest of two choice.

independent_check.passage: The large temple bell is heavy, but the handbell is _____.
independent_check.prompt: Write the correct comparative form of light.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a superlative in a setting without bells.
transfer_check.passage: Of the four routes, the riverside path has the least traffic.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence saying it is the safest route.

concept_slots.description: uses the word safest
states that the riverside path or route is safest

levels.title: Explain an honest decision
levels.focus: summarise a moral problem and justify a response in own words
levels.teaching_goal: Write a concise response that identifies the conflict, chooses an honest action, and supports it with evidence.

guided_check.teaching_block: A strong moral response names the action and why it is right. Worked example: 'She should return the key because it belongs to another family.'
guided_check.passage: Tara finds a house key labelled with her neighbour's flat number.
guided_check.prompt: Which response includes both an action and a reason?
options: Tara should return the key because her neighbour owns it.
accepted_answers: Tara should return the key because her neighbour owns it.

bridge.teaching_block: Build the response from three parts: what happened, what should be done, why that action is fair.
bridge.passage: A cashier forgets to include a notebook on Hari's bill.
bridge.prompt: Which action belongs in the middle of the response?
options: Hari should point out the missing notebook.
accepted_answers: Hari should point out the missing notebook.

masterclass.teaching_block: Honesty is not the same as avoiding punishment. A sound reason focuses on truth, ownership, or fairness, even when nobody is watching.
masterclass.passage: No one sees Anvi find a classmate's badge.
masterclass.prompt: Which reason best supports returning it?
options: The badge belongs to someone else.
accepted_answers: The badge belongs to someone else.

independent_check.teaching_block: Respond in your own words to this unseen dilemma.
independent_check.passage: A delivery rider gives Kabir two parcels, but one has another family's name and address.
independent_check.prompt: Summarise the problem and explain what Kabir should do.

concept_slots.description: states that one parcel belongs to another family
says to return, refuse, or alert the rider
links the action to honesty or ownership

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply honest reasoning to shared information.
transfer_check.passage: Niya is accidentally added to a private class chat meant for another section. She can read messages that were not sent to her.
transfer_check.prompt: In your own words, explain the responsible action and why it matters.

concept_slots.description: suggests leaving, not reading, and/or informing a teacher
explains privacy, trust, or wrong audience

items.passage: At a bakery, Om noticed the cashier had returned an extra note. He gave it back before leaving.
items.prompt: Which main idea fits best?
options: Om chooses honesty over keeping extra money.
accepted_answers: Om chooses honesty over keeping extra money.

items.passage: Sana cracked a borrowed plant pot while moving it. She told the owner and offered a replacement.
items.prompt: State what Sana's actions show and cite one action.

concept_slots.description: identifies honesty or responsibility
mentions telling the owner or replacing the pot

items.passage: A boy found a wallet, checked the identity card, and handed it to a police officer.
items.prompt: Which detail most strongly supports an inference of honesty?
options: He handed the wallet to a police officer.
The wallet had an identity card.
accepted_answers: He handed the wallet to a police officer.

items.passage: A student sees her score was added incorrectly in her favour and asks the teacher to check it.
items.prompt: Explain the main message of this event.

concept_slots.description: states that honesty means correcting a helpful mistake
refers to reporting or checking the score

items.passage: Events: Reva returned a scarf; Reva saw a name tag; Reva found the scarf.
items.prompt: Which happened first?

items.passage: Events: the coach corrected the result; Tenzin admitted crossing the line early; the race ended.
items.prompt: Put the events in logical order.
accepted_answers: the race ended, Tenzin admitted crossing the line early, the coach corrected the result
the race ended; Tenzin admitted crossing the line early; the coach corrected the result
race ended, Tenzin admitted, coach corrected

items.passage: First Ira counted the change. Next she noticed an extra coin. Finally she returned it.
items.prompt: What happened immediately before Ira returned the coin?

items.passage: Events: Jay informed the librarian; Jay discovered a torn page; Jay opened the borrowed book.
items.prompt: Arrange the events from first to last.
accepted_answers: Jay opened the borrowed book, Jay discovered a torn page, Jay informed the librarian
Jay opened the borrowed book; Jay discovered a torn page; Jay informed the librarian
opened book, discovered torn page, informed librarian

items.passage: The guard was vigilant, but the sleepy visitor noticed nothing.
items.prompt: What does vigilant mean?

items.passage: The room was chaotic before the shelves were arranged; afterwards it was orderly.
items.prompt: Write the opposite of chaotic from the sentence.

items.passage: Rafi gave a sincere apology: he named his mistake and did not make excuses.
items.prompt: Which meaning fits sincere?

items.passage: The brittle string snapped, while the flexible cord bent without breaking.
items.prompt: Use the contrast to explain brittle.

items.passage: Two bells weigh 60 g and 95 g.
items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: The 60 g bell is lightest of two.
The 60 g bell is more lighter.

items.passage: A copper bell is bright, but a polished silver bell reflects more light.
items.prompt: Complete the comparison: The silver bell is _____.

items.passage: Four ribbons are 10 cm, 14 cm, 18 cm, and 22 cm long.
items.prompt: How should the 22 cm ribbon be described?
options: It is the longer ribbon of four.
It is the most long ribbon.

items.passage: Three routes take 8, 11, and 15 minutes.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence about the 8-minute route using quickest.

concept_slots.description: uses quickest
states that the 8-minute route is quickest

items.passage: A waiter gives Pia another table's change.
items.prompt: Which response is most honest?
options: Pia should return it because it belongs to another customer.
Pia should hide it under a plate.
accepted_answers: Pia should return it because it belongs to another customer.

items.passage: Nakul notices that a library book was already torn when he borrowed it.
items.prompt: Summarise the problem and explain a responsible action.

concept_slots.description: states that the borrowed book has damage
suggests promptly telling or showing the librarian
connects the action to honesty or avoiding blame

items.passage: A game awards Leena a point that she knows she did not earn.
items.prompt: Which reason best supports speaking up?
options: A fair score must record what really happened.
accepted_answers: A fair score must record what really happened.

items.passage: A child receives a message containing another pupil's test answers by mistake.
items.prompt: In your own words, explain what the child should do and why.

concept_slots.description: suggests not using or sharing the answers and informing an adult
explains fairness, privacy, or cheating
